key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court held that the Adoption Assistance and Child Welfare Act's requirement that states make reasonable efforts to prevent removal and reunify families creates no right enforceable by private individuals under section 1983 or directly under the Act.
key_cases.relevance: It is the controlling holding that federal child welfare compliance is enforced through funding, not private suit.
key_cases.quote: We hold that the Act does not create an enforceable right on behalf of respondents.

key_cases.case_name: DeShaney v. Winnebago County Department of Social Services
key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court held that a state's failure to protect a child from violence by his father, even after repeated reports and agency monitoring, is not a deprivation of liberty under the Due Process Clause, because the Clause imposes no general affirmative duty to protect.
key_cases.relevance: It confirms that federal constitutional law does not itself enforce agency performance standards.
key_cases.quote: As a general matter, then, we conclude that a State's failure to protect an individual against private violence simply does not constitute a violation of the Due Process Clause.
